Consult Summary:
- Acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by a recent viral upper respiratory infection, with chest tightness, wheeze, and shortness of breath; patient is currently out of inhalers; plan includes reliever and controller inhalers, a short course of oral steroids, spacer device, and temporary activity/work leave with safety guidance.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Chest tightness for approximately 3 hours, with wheeze and shortness of breath; accompanying cough; recent cold symptoms (sore throat, runny nose) starting last week; runny nose improving but cough persists.
- Onset/Timeline: Symptoms began about 3 hours ago and have been ongoing; prior URI symptoms since last week; runny nose improving while cough and chest tightness persist.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors: Exertion (walking up stairs) increases shortness of breath; patient has not used inhalers in about a week due to being away at university and running out.
- Associated symptoms: Sore throat, runny nose; hay fever symptoms.
- Systems review (respiratory): Wheeze, non-productive cough, shortness of breath on exertion but not at rest.
- Past Medical History: Asthma (longstanding; history of a severe exacerbation in adolescence requiring hospitalization with airway intubation). Also history of eczema; hay fever; dust allergy; milk protein allergy in childhood.
- Medications: Ventolin (Salbutamol) inhaler and Clenil Modulite inhaler previously; currently out of inhalers and not using them in the past week.
- Allergies: No drug allergies reported. Allergic history includes dust sensitivity and hay fever; milk protein allergy in childhood.
- Social History: Not explicitly detailed; patient was at university last week; plan includes a period of rest and possible time off work (self-certification for seven days).
- Family History: Mother with eczema; father with asthma; history of eczema in childhood.

Past Medical History (reiterated): Asthma; eczema (childhood); dust and milk protein allergies; hay fever; family history of asthma and eczema.

Medications:
- Ventolin (Salbutamol) inhaler — not currently available; not in use in past week.
- Clenil Modulite inhaler — not currently available; not in use in past week.
- No drug allergies reported.

- Occupational: Not specified; plan includes potential time off work.
- Tobacco, alcohol, drugs: Not specified.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1:
- Assessment: Acute asthma exacerbation likely part of current viral URI, with chest tightness, wheeze, and exertional shortness of breath; cough non-productive; nocturnal symptoms not clearly described but cough persists.
- Plan:
  - Prescribe inhaled reliever: Ventolin (Salbutamol) inhaler.
  - Prescribe inhaled controller: Clenil Modulite inhaler.
  - Provide spacer device and instructions for use (priming, inhalation with spacer, breathing technique).
  - Short course of oral steroids: five days; two tablets in the morning (name of steroid not specified).
  - After recovery, resume Clenil Modulite in the morning with Ventolin PRN.
  - Advise patient to monitor symptoms and seek medical attention if Ventolin is needed more than every 3 hours or if there is deterioration (e.g., increased shortness of breath, chest tightness, dizziness).
  - Advise rest; potential time off work with self-certification for seven days.

Issue 2:
- Assessment: Maintenance therapy optimization for asthma after acute episode.
- Plan:
  - Continue/restart Clenil Modulite in the morning and Ventolin PRN once stabilized.
  - Spacer to be used with inhalers; provide instructions.
  - Ensure patient knows when to seek care if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

Issue 3:
- Assessment: Safety and return-to-function considerations.
- Plan:
  - Self-certification for seven days off work; rest until feeling better.
  - Return for follow-up or if symptoms worsen.
  - Provided education on when to seek urgent care (worsening SOB, chest pain, lightheadedness).
